title: O That I Could Repent
description: O That I Could Repent in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 102.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: O that I could re-pent! With all my i-dols part, And to thy gra-cious eye pre_-sent A hum-ble, con-trite heart; A heart with grief op-prest For hav-ing grieved my God, A trou-bled heart that can-not rest, Till sprin-kled with thy blood.

lines: And to thy gracious eye present
A troubled heart that cannot rest,
Strike with thy love's resistless stroke,
And break this heart of stone!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
